2608.29959.title: Generative vs. Encoder Models for Multilingual NER: A Comprehensive Empirical Study on Naamapadam
2608.29959.paper_summary: Language is humanity's most consequential technology, yet for over a billion speakers across India's twenty-two constitutionally recognised languages, its digital layer remains structurally incomplete. Named Entity Recognition (NER), the foundational step in transforming raw text into machine-interpretable knowledge, has been studied exhaustively for English but remains largely unsolved across most Indic languages. This paper presents a rigorous comparative study of generative and encoder-based neural architectures for NER on all eleven languages of the Naamapadam benchmark. We evaluate five classic model families spanning sequence-to-sequence transformers and multilingual encoders; four decoder-only large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned with LoRA and 4-bit NF4 quantisation; and nine generative models in zero-to-5-shot inference. Under strict CoNLL span-level evaluation, encoder-based models (mBERT and XLM-R, both F1=0.675 on Hindi) substantially outperform every generative architecture in ten of eleven languages, with gaps of 7.5-40 percentage points against the strongest competitor (Gemma-2-2B: avg F1=0.427). The best few-shot result reaches only 28% of the encoder baseline. We identify three language clusters--encoder-dominant, partial-coverage, and failure-zone; and provide actionable deployment guidelines grounded in transfer learning and low-resource NLP principles.
2608.29959.paper_summary_zh: 語言是人類最重要的技術，然而對於印度二十二種憲法認可的語言中的十億多講者來說，其數位層仍然結構不完整。命名實體識別（NER）是將原始文本轉換為機器可解釋知識的基礎步驟，對於英語已經進行了廣泛的研究，但在大多數印度語言中仍然基本未解決。本文對Naamapadam基準的所有十一種語言進行了生成式和編碼器基礎神經架構的嚴謹比較研究。我們評估了五個經典模型系列，涵蓋序列到序列的Transformer和多語言編碼器；四個僅解碼的大型語言模型（LLMs），使用LoRA和4位NF4量化進行微調；以及九個在零到五次推理中的生成模型。在嚴格的CoNLL範圍級評估下，基於編碼器的模型（mBERT和XLM-R，兩者在印地語上的F1=0.675）在十一種語言中的十種中顯著超越了每個生成架構，與最強競爭對手（Gemma-2-2B：平均F1=0.427）之間的差距為7.5-40個百分點。最佳的少樣本結果僅達到編碼器基線的28%。我們識別出三個語言集群——編碼器主導、部分覆蓋和失敗區；並提供基於轉移學習和低資源NLP原則的可行部署指南。
